title: A/B test readout for a pricing page
prompt:
Kestrel Notes tested a new pricing page for four weeks. The product manager wants to ship variant B on Monday and has asked you for the readout. You are supplied the test plan written before launch and the weekly results as CSV. Every figure you cite must come from the supplied files.

Use these definitions exactly:
- Signup rate = signups ÷ visitors, per variant, over all four weeks and both devices.
- Relative lift = variant B's signup rate ÷ control's signup rate − 1.
- The sample-ratio check compares the visitors each variant actually received with the 50/50 split the plan called for, using a chi-square statistic: the sum over both variants of (observed − expected)² ÷ expected.
- The significance test for the primary metric is a two-sided, pooled two-proportion z-test.

Write the readout: the result on the primary metric, whether the test can be trusted and why, what the test does and does not show, and a clear recommendation with the next step. For anything you find wrong with how the test ran, point to the rows of the results that show it. Write it for a product manager who wants a decision.

End the readout with an answer block in exactly this format, one line per answer. Each line is the label, a colon, and the number alone: no words, no working and no second number. A currency sign, thousands separators and a percent sign are fine.

A1: <total visitors in control>
A2: <total visitors in variant B>
A3: <control signup rate, as a percentage to two decimals>
A4: <variant B signup rate, as a percentage to two decimals>
A5: <relative lift of variant B over control, as a percentage to one decimal>
A6: <chi-square statistic of the sample-ratio check, to one decimal>
A7: <two-sided p-value of the primary-metric test, to three decimals>

This is an internal readout. Fetch nothing external and do not invent benchmarks.

completion.check: The response ends with the required answer block and all 7 labeled answers A1-A7 are present, each on its own line with the number alone.
A1 states the total visitors in control over the four weeks; full credit within 0.1%, zero credit beyond 10% off.
A2 states the total visitors in variant B over the four weeks; full credit within 0.1%, zero credit beyond 10% off.
A3 states control's signup rate as a percentage; full credit within 0.02, zero credit 0.5 or more off.
A4 states variant B's signup rate as a percentage; full credit within 0.02, zero credit 0.5 or more off.
A5 states variant B's relative lift over control as a percentage; full credit within 0.15, zero credit 3 or more off.
A6 states the chi-square statistic of observed visitors against the planned 50/50 split; full credit within 2%, zero credit beyond 30% off.

A7 states the two-sided p-value of the pooled two-proportion test on signup rate (a continuity-corrected test lands inside the full-credit band); full credit within 0.015, zero credit 0.1 or more off.
The readout gives one clear recommendation on whether to ship variant B now. No recommendation, or one that leaves the decision open, fails.

skill_adherence.check: The readout says the split of visitors (12,480 control against 11,020 variant B) departs from the planned 50/50 by more than chance allows, and that the comparison between the variants cannot be trusted until that is explained. Reporting the two totals without saying the comparison is unreliable fails.
The readout states that the difference in signup rate is not statistically significant at the plan's 5% level.
The readout notes that neither variant reached the 18,000 visitors the plan required before the result is read.

Every rate, count, statistic and p-value presented as a result is derivable from the results file, and every figure about the plan matches the test plan. The readout states no projected revenue, annualised gain or industry benchmark as if it were data.

best_practices.check: The readout does not call variant B the winner and does not recommend shipping it on the strength of this test.
The paid-conversion difference is not used to justify shipping variant B or to claim an effect. If it is mentioned, it is described as the secondary metric the plan said is not a decision metric.

The readout says which rows of the results show the imbalance: the mobile rows, where variant B has 5,400 visitors against control's 6,900 (desktop is balanced, 5,620 against 5,580). Naming mobile is enough; not saying where the imbalance is fails.

The next step includes checking how visitors are assigned to or served variant B and correcting what is found before the test is rerun or read again. It fails if the only next step is to keep the test running, collect more data, or ship.
